clue.text: Caught about fifty, but seemed far from pleased

indicators.note: about means the word for caught goes around the letter for fifty

parts.note: caught as in trapped means snared
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A cricketer caught out for fifty walks off looking far from pleased.
explanation.definitionFit: To growl with bared teeth is a plain show of displeasure, the past tense matching seemed.

clue.text: Getting rid of the coarse stuff

explanation.surface: Throwing out the rough material.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacking is dismissal from a job, and also coarse cloth woven for bags.

clue.text: Judge appearing in new bar attire

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of bar attire are made into something new

explanation.surface: A judge turns up in fresh court dress.
explanation.definitionFit: To arbitrate is to settle a dispute as an impartial referee.

clue.text: Continental university that's superior

explanation.surface: A European university claims to be better than others.
explanation.definitionFit: Liège in Belgium has a university; a liege is a feudal superior or lord.

clue.text: Grapes aid restoration when run down

indicators.note: restoration means the letters of grapes aid are rebuilt in a different order

explanation.surface: Grape juice helps a worn-out person recover.
explanation.definitionFit: To disparage is to belittle or speak slightingly of something.

clue.text: Hit the drink to get sympathy

parts.note: to hit is to rap
port is a fortified wine, a drink

explanation.surface: Someone thumps the table, then takes a drink, to win fellow feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapport is a close, understanding relationship, a mutual fellow feeling.

clue.text: The King, soon talked incessantly

parts.note: R, for Rex, stands for a king
anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: The monarch soon chattered without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: To run on is to keep talking at length without a pause.

clue.text: Hand round games — travellers need them

indicators.note: round means the word for hand goes around the word for games

parts.note: to hand something over is to pass it
sport is games played

explanation.surface: Someone hands out games to people setting off on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Passports are official travel documents needed for crossing borders.

clue.text: Some food our noses detect

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Our noses pick up the smell of some food.
explanation.definitionFit: A smell is what the nose senses; the clue's phrase stands for a thing smelt.

clue.text: Ramblers may well be dependent on it

definitions.text: Ramblers may well be dependent on it

parts.words: Ramblers may well be dependent on it
parts.note: ramblers here are rambling roses, climbing plants that lean on a garden frame for support, not hikers

explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a lattice framework that supports climbing plants.

clue.text: Rope which is about adequate

able means competent or adequate

explanation.surface: Someone asks which rope is long enough for the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable is a thick, strong line, a heavy rope used on ships.

clue.text: The craft holds with pitch being used in building

parts.note: SS, steamship, is a vessel or craft
and joins things, as with does
the pitch of a sound is its tone

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' looks like tar in a shipyard; it is the musical sense, TONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandstone is a sedimentary rock widely quarried as a building material.

clue.text: Where to find fighting cocks usually

explanation.surface: Someone explains where cockfighting birds are to be found most of the time.
explanation.definitionFit: A main is a cockfighting match, so birds fighting are in one; the phrase also means mostly, on the whole.

clue.text: A supernatural being left in some danger

explanation.definitionFit: Peril is serious risk, a synonym for danger.

clue.text: People may well look into it and reflect

definitions.text: People may well look into it

explanation.surface: People gaze into a well and think things over.
explanation.definitionFit: A looking-glass is a mirror people look into; to glass is an old verb meaning to mirror or reflect.

clue.text: He objects to laying out money to film Welsh town

definitions.text: He objects to laying out money

parts.note: a skin is a thin layer or film
Flint is a town in north Wales

explanation.surface: A miser objects to paying for a film about a town in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser hates spending cash, which is what a skinflint is.

clue.text: Sounds like a rider admitting fuming

parts.note: as means like, in comparison

indicators.note: admitting means the rider's letters let the word for fuming inside

parts.note: a rider is an addition to a document, as a PS (postscript) is
fuming means angry, irate

explanation.surface: Someone sounds like a jockey who admits to being furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider' suggests a horseman; it is an added note to a letter, PS.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics an aspirate is a breathy sound such as H, so these are sounds.

clue.text: A right not exercised in a boy's support

clue.text: Mild, though consumed with fury initially

indicators.note: initially means the word for fury comes at the start

consumed means ate

explanation.definitionFit: Temperate means moderate, as a mild climate is.

clue.text: The chief executive pretends to be prepared to receive one

to be prepared means the letters of pretends are to be made up afresh

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.walkthrough: 'to be prepared' rearranges PRETENDS into PRESDENT, and 'to receive' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A president is the head of state in a republic, its top executive officer.

clue.text: Dominate law-men by craft

parts.note: a posse is a band of men gathered to enforce the law
SS, steamship, is a craft

explanation.surface: Lawmen gain control by cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like cunning; it is a ship, SS.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess someone is to control them completely, as a spirit does.

clue.text: A short time in South America or South Sea islands

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time

clue.text: Appeal to the country to support a trusted leader

leader means the first letter of trusted

clue.text: Small county suffering cut in personnel

explanation.definitionFit: Staff are the employees of an organisation, its personnel.

clue.text: A couple of hundred big guns in the capital

clue.text: Landseer's resort — 11

explanation.walkthrough: The 11 refers to IN THE MAIN, meaning at sea. Landseer was a Victorian animal painter, which hides the land-seer reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A crow's nest is the lookout platform high on a ship's mast, used for sighting land.

clue.text: A key locks, such furniture

parts.note: C is a musical key
locks are tresses of hair

reordered means the letters of ale and are put in a new order

clue.text: Ring a poor actor back in the USA
